speaker_role: essay coach at consultancy (College Essay Guy); references what admissions officers have told him
commercial_incentive: Sells one-on-one coaching and guides, though mentions free spots.
key_insights: Selective colleges use supplements to assess fit to major and campus culture, demonstrated interest, and fit with institutional priorities.
Save time with a 'super essay': track all prompts in a spreadsheet, group by type, and reuse one core essay across similar prompts.
A why-this-college essay is a research essay; alternate between specific school offerings and specific facts about yourself.
For why-major essays, focus on the last three to five years and avoid claiming a lifelong fixed major.
For community or diversity prompts, diversity is broader than race; pair three to five specific campus things with three to five ways you'd contribute.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Supplements typically run 200 to 650 words, per speaker.
Example: 12 schools at two to three essays each implies 24 to 36 essays.
Speaker says the super-essay approach saves 20-plus hours.
notable_or_distinctive: The essay-tracker and prompt-grouping method for reducing workload.
reliability_notes: Claim that demonstrated interest and priorities can be difference makers rests on unnamed admissions officers; some sales framing.
